A game whose\n    ///      entry is custody of a token calls {_takeSeat} from wherever\n    ///      custody is taken instead, and never funds a reserve.\n    ///\n    ///      UNDER A CLOSED ROSTER a funded reserve is a SEAT ({_openRoster}):\n    ///      refused once the game has started or when every seat is taken,\n    ///      and waited for only from the start.\n    function _addToReserve(uint256 player, uint256 amount) internal {\n        uint256 newAmount = CommitReveal.deposit(player, amount);\n        if (newAmount != 0) {\n            _takeSeat(player);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Debit a reserve on its owner's request; emptying it is leaving.\n    /// @dev Leaving settles nothing and costs nothing beyond the departure:\n    ///      leaving the set the cycle waits for and being punished for going\n    ///      silent are different questions, and only the first is the cycle's.\n    function _withdrawFromReserve(uint256 player, uint256 amount) internal {\n        uint256 newAmount = CommitReveal.withdraw(player, amount);\n        if (newAmount == 0) {\n            _leaveSeat(player);\n        }\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // A CLOSED ROSTER\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Make this a game for a fixed set of members: `seats` of them,\n    ///         seated by funding a reserve, started by `creator`, ending\n    ///         `cycles` cycles after its start, with `options` for the game.\n    /// @dev OPT-IN, AND ONCE. A game that never calls this (the persistent\n    ///      world) has open entry, exactly as before rosters existed. A game\n    ///      cloned per table calls it from its initialiser, in the same\n    ///      transaction as the clone is made, so nobody can open it first.\n    ///\n    ///      The roster's rules, in one place: a seat is taken by funding a\n    ///      reserve while the game has not started and a seat is free; a\n    ///      seated member may top up at any time; emptying a reserve is\n    ///      leaving (before the start the seat can be taken again, after it\n    ///      nobody joins); the creator starts the game once two are seated\n    ///      ({_startGame}), and may forfeit a member who has not acted\n    ///      ({_forfeitMember}); after its last cycle nobody commits, advances\n    ///      or is forfeited ({_hasEnded}), while that cycle's reveals and every\n    ///      missed reveal's settlement still go through.\n    function _openRoster(\n        address creator,\n        uint8 seats,\n        uint16 cycles,\n        bytes32 options\n    ) internal {\n        CommitReveal.openRoster(creator, seats, cycles, options);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Seat a player, and wait for them if the game has started (or\n    ///         has open entry). What a custody game calls where it takes\n    ///         custody, in place of {_startWaitingFor}.\n    function _takeSeat(uint256 player) internal {\n        if (CommitReveal.seat(player)) {\n            CommitReveal.startWaitingFor(player);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Leave: stop waiting for this player and free their seat.\n    function _leaveSeat(uint256 player) internal {\n        CommitReveal.releaseSeat(player);\n        CommitReveal.stopWaitingFor(player);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Start a game with a closed roster.\n    /// @param sender Who is starting it, normally `msg.sender`: the creator,\n    ///        or a delegate of theirs (their browser's key).\n    function _startGame(address sender) internal returns (uint64 cycleNumber) {\n        Delegation.requireAccountFor(sender, _requireRosterCreator());\n        return\n            CommitReveal.start(\n                _clock(),\n                _cycle(),\n                CYCLE_POLICY == CyclePolicy.Manual ? 0 : _timestamp()\n            );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The creator's forfeit of a member who has not acted in the\n    ///         current phase. See {CommitReveal-forfeitMember}.\n    /// @param sender Who is forfeiting, normally `msg.sender`: the creator,\n    ///        or a delegate of theirs.\n    function _forfeitMember(address sender, uint256 player) internal {\n        Delegation.requireAccountFor(sender, _requireRosterCreator());\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting) = _cycleNumber();\n        CommitReveal.forfeitMember(player, cycleNumber, commiting);\n    }\n\n    function _roster() internal view returns (Roster memory) {\n        return CommitReveal.roster();\n    }\n\n    function _members() internal view returns (uint256[] memory) {\n        return CommitReveal.members();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice WHAT THE GAME READS AT THIS TABLE, as its creator chose it.\n    /// @dev Opaque to the base, and the only way a game's routes learn\n    ///      anything chosen at creation: each route is its own contract\n    ///      behind the router, so the lobby's route cannot call a game's hook.\n    ///      A game decodes it in its own routes (and refuses what it cannot\n    ///      read); zero under open entry, and wherever the creator sent none.\n    function _gameOptions() internal view returns (bytes32) {\n        return CommitReveal.gameOptions();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice THE END'S HOOK: the last cycle this game plays, or zero if it\n    ///         has none (open entry, or a roster not started yet).\n    function _lastCycleNumber() internal view returns (uint64) {\n        return CommitReveal.lastCycleNumber();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice THE END'S HOOK: whether the game has played its last cycle.\n    /// @dev A comparison, never an event: nothing runs at the moment a game\n    ///      ends, so a game's own routes (a settlement, a score) ask this.\n    function _hasEnded() internal view returns (bool) {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, ) = _cycleNumber();\n        return CommitReveal.isPastTheEnd(cycleNumber);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev The creator, or a revert: under open entry there is nobody to\n    ///      ask, and `Delegation` would read a zero creator as \"the sender\".\n    function _requireRosterCreator() private view returns (address) {\n        Roster memory opened = CommitReveal.roster();\n        if (opened.seats == 0) {\n            revert NoRoster();\n        }\n        return opened.creator;\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // WHO THE CYCLE WAITS FOR\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Start blocking the cycle on this player. Idempotent.\n    function _startWaitingFor(uint256 player) internal {\n        CommitReveal.startWaitingFor(player);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Stop blocking the cycle on this player. Idempotent.\n    function _stopWaitingFor(uint256 player) internal {\n        CommitReveal.stopWaitingFor(player);\n    }\n\n    function _isWaitedFor(uint256 player) internal view returns (bool) {\n        return CommitReveal.isWaitedFor(player);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The denominator, and how much of it has acted this cycle.\n    function _attendance(\n        uint64 cycleNumber\n    ) internal view returns (Attendance memory) {\n        return CommitReveal.attendance(cycleNumber);\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // COMMIT / REVEAL\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function _commitmentOf(\n        uint256 player\n    ) internal view returns (Commitment memory) {\n        return CommitReveal.commitmentOf(player);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Bond part of a reserve to a turn this cycle. `player` must\n    ///         already be resolved by {_playerOf}.\n    function _makeCommitment(\n        uint256 player,\n        bytes24 commitmentHash,\n        uint256 bond\n    ) internal {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting) = _cycleNumber();\n        CommitReveal.commit(\n            player,\n            commitmentHash,\n            bond,\n            cycleNumber,\n            commiting\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Take a commitment back while its commit phase is still open.\n    ///         `player` must already be resolved by {_playerOf}.\n    function _cancelCommitment(uint256 player) internal {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting) = _cycleNumber();\n        CommitReveal.cancel(player, cycleNumber, commiting);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Check one chunk of a reveal, before the game resolves it.\n    /// @param digest The game's hash of the chunk, in the one encoding:\n    ///        `bytes24(keccak256(abi.encode(secret, actions, furtherActions)))`.\n    /// @param numActions How many actions the chunk carries.\n    /// @param furtherActions The hash of the next chunk, or zero for the last.\n    /// @return chunk What {_closeChunk} needs once the game has resolved it.\n    /// @dev ANYONE MAY REVEAL, which is why this takes no sender: a reveal is\n    ///      validated by the hash, and accepting it from anyone is what stops\n    ///      an offline player forfeiting.\n    ///\n    ///      ORDER INDEPENDENCE IS THE GAME'S TO KEEP between this call and the\n    ///      next. Reveals arrive in whatever order the mempool delivers them,\n    ///      and the board after a cycle must not depend on that: accumulate,\n    ///      never branch on what another reveal of the same cycle could have\n    ///      changed. See `AGENTS.md`, \"Commit-reveal rules\".\n    function _openChunk(\n        uint256 player,\n        bytes24 digest,\n        uint256 numActions,\n        bytes24 furtherActions\n    ) internal view returns (CommitReveal.Chunk memory chunk) {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting) = _cycleNumber();\n        return\n            CommitReveal.openChunk(\n                player,\n                cycleNumber,\n                commiting,\n                digest,\n                numActions,\n                furtherActions,\n                ACTIONS_PER_REVEAL\n            );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Check one chunk of a MISSED reveal: a commitment whose cycle is\n    ///         over, settled by being shown what it committed to.\n    /// @dev ANYONE MAY SETTLE THIS WAY, because nothing in it can hurt the\n    ///      player more than their own silence already has: the chain checks\n    ///      that the chunks are exactly what was committed, the game takes its\n    ///      penalty for exactly those actions, and the surplus of the bond goes\n    ///      back to the player. Nobody but the player receives anything, so a\n    ///      stranger settling gains nothing either, which is what makes it safe\n    ///      to leave open. Who can is whoever holds the chunks: the player's\n    ///      own client, a reveal service, a world playing its own seats.\n    ///\n    ///      Why it exists at all: a bond may exceed what the turn costs, since a\n    ///      bond equal to the exact cost tells everyone how many actions the\n    ///      commitment hides. Without the chunks the contract cannot tell the\n    ///      surplus from the stake, so forfeiting all of it would punish the\n    ///      hiding rather than the silence. See {_forfeitMissedReveal} for the\n    ///      settlement that is not shown the chunks.\n    function _openMissedChunk(\n        uint256 player,\n        bytes24 digest,\n        uint256 numActions,\n        bytes24 furtherActions\n    ) internal view returns (CommitReveal.Chunk memory chunk) {\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, ) = _cycleNumber();\n        return\n            CommitReveal.openMissedChunk(\n                player,\n                cycleNumber,\n                digest,\n                numActions,\n                furtherActions,\n                ACTIONS_PER_REVEAL\n            );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Apply an opened chunk: charge its cost (a reveal) or forfeit\n    ///         its penalty (a missed reveal), and move the chain on.\n    /// @param amount For a reveal, what the game's resolution reports the\n    ///        chunk cost, taken from the bond and the reserve; a chunk costing\n    ///        more than the bond still holds is refused. For a missed reveal,\n    ///        the game's penalty for the chunk's actions, capped at the bond\n    ///        and handed to {_forfeit}.\n    /// @return taken What was charged, or what {_forfeit} took.\n    function _closeChunk(\n        CommitReveal.Chunk memory chunk,\n        uint256 amount\n    ) internal returns (uint256 taken) {\n        if (!chunk.missed) {\n            CommitReveal.closeRevealedChunk(chunk, amount);\n            return amount;\n        }\n        uint256 charged = CommitReveal.closeMissedChunk(chunk, amount);\n        taken = _forfeit(chunk.player, charged);\n        emit CommitmentVoid(\n            chunk.player,\n            chunk.cycleNumber,\n            chunk.commitmentHash,\n            chunk.furtherActions,\n            taken\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Settle a missed reveal WITHOUT its chunks: the whole remaining\n    ///         bond is forfeited.\n    /// @param sender Who is settling, normally `msg.sender`.\n    /// @param id The identity, as the client named it.\n    /// @dev ONLY THE PLAYER OR THEIR DELEGATE, resolved here through\n    ///      {_playerOf} so that no route can skip it. A stranger could\n    ///      otherwise take a bond whose surplus the player could have\n    ///      recovered by settling with the chunks. A player who has lost their\n    ///      plan, or who simply wants to play again, still has this route, and\n    ///      it is always available: it needs nothing but the identity.\n    ///\n    ///      LIVENESS IS UNCHANGED BY IT. A member whose past commitment nobody\n    ///      settles cannot commit, so the cycle waits for them exactly as for a\n    ///      member who does not commit: under a timed policy the clock moves on\n    ///      and only early advance is lost.\n    function _forfeitMissedReveal(address sender, uint256 id) internal {\n        uint256 player = _playerOf(sender, id);\n        (uint64 cycleNumber, ) = _cycleNumber();\n        (bytes24 head, uint256 bond) = CommitReveal.voidCommitment(\n            player,\n            cycleNumber\n        );\n        uint256 forfeited = _forfeit(player, bond);\n        emit CommitmentVoid(player, cycleNumber, head, bytes24(0), forfeited);\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // ADVANCING THE CYCLE\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice Move the cycle on, if the rules already permit it.\n    /// @dev ITS OWN TRANSACTION, NEVER A RIDER ON THE LAST REVEAL: advancing\n    ///      inside a reveal would make that call mean something different\n    ///      depending on whether you happened to be last, would make its gas\n    ///      depend on winning a race, and would not be retriable. Permissionless\n    ///      but strictly conditional, so letting anyone call it grants nothing.\n    ///      See {CommitReveal-advance} for unanimity and for why it only ever\n    ///      widens a window.\n    function _advanceCycle()\n        internal\n        returns (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting)\n    {\n        return\n            CommitReveal.advance(\n                _clock(),\n                _cycle(),\n                CYCLE_POLICY == CyclePolicy.Manual ? 0 : _timestamp()\n            );\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // THE SEAMS\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// @notice WHO THE CALLER IS ACTING FOR, having checked that they may.\n    /// @param sender The account or key that sent the transaction.\n    /// @param id The identity, as the client named it.\n    /// @return player The identity this action is filed under, which is what\n    ///         every record in {CommitReveal} is keyed by.\n    /// @dev THE DEFAULT IS AN ADDRESS GAME: the identity is the account, and\n    ///      the only question is authority, answered by the delegation\n    ///      library, so a local signer may act for the account that authorised\n    ///      it. A token game overrides this to resolve a token and check that\n    ///      the caller may act for its owner. RESOLUTION AND AUTHORITY ARE ONE\n    ///      FUNCTION ON PURPOSE: splitting them would let a caller reach a\n    ///      resolved identity without having passed the check.\n    function _playerOf(\n        address sender,\n        uint256 id\n    ) internal view virtual returns (uint256 player) {\n        // An identity that is not an address CANNOT BE ONE HERE: two ids that\n        // differ above the 160th bit would otherwise be the same player,\n        // sharing one reserve and one commitment, with nothing raised anywhere.\n        if (id > type(uint160).max) {\n            revert InvalidPlayer(id);\n        }\n        // Zero means \"whoever is calling\", which the library resolves.\n        return\n            uint256(\n                uint160(\n                    Delegation.requireAccountFor(sender, address(uint160(id)))\n                )\n            );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice WHAT NOT REVEALING COSTS.\n    /// @param amount What the settlement says is at stake: the game's penalty\n    ///        for the chunks it was shown, or the whole remaining bond when it\n    ///        was shown none.\n    /// @return forfeited How much of it was taken, for the event.\n    /// @dev The framework's only requirement is that SOMETHING is lost: a\n    ///      player who dislikes what they committed to can always go quiet.\n    ///      The default takes the amount out of the reserve and leaves it in\n    ///      the contract. A game whose stake is custody of a token seizes the\n    ///      token here instead and returns zero - on BOTH settlement routes,\n    ///      since a custody game bonds nothing and \"only the penalty for what\n    ///      was committed\" would otherwise cost a player nothing.\n    ///\n    ///      NOTHING FORFEITED GOES TO WHOEVER SETTLED. A settler that could\n    ///      profit would race the player for their own surplus.\n    function _forfeit(\n        uint256 player,\n        uint256 amount\n    ) internal virtual returns (uint256 forfeited) {\n        return CommitReveal.debit(player, amount);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice WHERE THE CYCLE IS. The seam the cycle policy varies at.\n    /// @dev The only thing about the clock that is virtual: a game with a\n    ///      fourth policy overrides this one function. {_cycleNumber} is\n    ///      derived from it rather than the other way round.\n    function _cycle() internal view virtual returns (Cycle memory) {\n        return\n            CommitReveal.cycle(\n                _clock(),\n                CYCLE_POLICY == CyclePolicy.Manual ? 0 : _timestamp()\n            );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The cycle as everything inside this contract asks about it.\n    /// @dev Deliberately NOT virtual: {_cycle} is the seam.\n    function _cycleNumber()\n        internal\n        view\n        returns (uint64 cycleNumber, bool commiting)\n    {\n        Cycle memory current = _cycle();\n        return (current.cycleNumber, current.commiting);\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // INTERNALS\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    function _clock() internal view returns (CommitReveal.Clock memory) {\n        return\n            CommitReveal.Clock({\n                policy: CYCLE_POLICY,\n                startTime: START_TIME,\n                commitPhaseDuration: COMMIT_PHASE_DURATION,\n                revealPhaseDuration: REVEAL_PHASE_DURATION\n            });\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The chain's time, or a test's.\n    function _timestamp() internal view returns (uint256) {\n        if (address(TIME) == address(0)) {\n            return block.timestamp;\n        }\n        return TIME.timestamp();\n    }\n}\n","keccak256":"0x51a932e6e94dbb958d7a74bd7197cfe428e314755bb8e50128d5175b269b9982","license":"AGPL-3.0"},"project/src/commit-reveal/interfaces/ICommitRevealLobby.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.21;\n\nimport {UsingCommitRevealTypes} from \"./UsingCommitRevealTypes.sol\";\n\n/// @title What a game for a fixed set of members exposes\n/// @notice The routes a game adds to be cloned per table by\n///         {CommitRevealGameFactory}: the initialiser the factory calls, the\n///         creator's two powers, and the roster as a client reads it. The rules\n///         are the base's ({UsingCommitReveal-_openRoster}); a game's route only\n///         forwards to them.\ninterface ICommitRevealLobby is UsingCommitRevealTypes {\n    /// @notice Give this game a closed roster of `seats`, created by `creator`,\n    ///         playing `cycles` cycles from its start, with the game's own\n    ///         `gameOptions` (opaque to the base; zero for none).\n    /// @dev Once. The factory calls it in the transaction that makes the\n    ///      clone, so nobody can open a clone's roster before it does.\n    function initializeLobby(\n        address creator,\n        uint8 seats,\n        uint16 cycles,\n        bytes32 gameOptions\n    ) external;\n\n    /// @notice Start the game: the creator (or a delegate of theirs), once two\n    ///         or more are seated. Closes the roster and re-anchors the clock.\n    function start() external returns (uint64 cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice Forfeit a member who has not committed in the current commit\n    ///         phase: the creator (or a delegate of theirs) only.\n    function forfeitMember(uint256 player) external;\n\n    /// @notice The roster, and who holds a seat.\n    function getRoster()\n        external\n        view\n        returns (Roster memory roster, uint256[] memory members);\n\n    /// @notice Where the game is against its end: the current cycle, the last\n    ///         it plays (zero before the start), and whether it is past it.\n    function getEnd()\n        external\n        view\n        returns (uint64 cycleNumber, uint64 lastCycleNumber, bool ended);\n\n    /// @notice Whether the game has played its last cycle.\n    function hasEnded() external view returns (bool);\n\n    /// @notice What the game's own rules read at this table, as created.\n    function getGameOptions() external view returns (bytes32);\n}\n","keccak256":"0xf0cf4c2589e71826b360f5c82c697ef7a2952352d6f489f78db782cc3e1d27ee","license":"MIT"},"project/src/commit-reveal/interfaces/UsingCommitRevealErrors.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.21;\n\n/// @title The errors of the commit-reveal base\n/// @dev Raised by {CommitReveal} and {UsingCommitReveal} through qualified\n///      names, and inherited by a game's own errors interface so that they are\n///      in the game's ABI where a client decodes them.\ninterface UsingCommitRevealErrors {\n    /// @notice the game has not started yet\n    error GameNotStarted();\n\n    /// @notice trying to commit while the reveal phase is running\n    error InRevealPhase(uint64 cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice trying to reveal while the commit phase is running\n    error InCommitmentPhase(uint64 cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice there is no commitment to reveal or to void\n    error NothingToReveal();\n\n    /// @notice there is no commitment to cancel\n    error NoCommitmentToCancel();\n\n    /// @notice an earlier commitment was never revealed; resolve it first\n    error PreviousCommitmentNotRevealed();\n\n    /// @notice the commitment belongs to a different cycle\n    error InvalidCycle(uint64 currentCycleNumber, uint64 commitmentCycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice the revealed chunk does not hash to the head of the chain\n    error CommitmentHashNotMatching();\n\n    /// @notice the player can still reveal, so the commitment cannot be voided\n    error CanStillReveal(uint64 cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice this identity cannot play this game\n    /// @dev What makes an identity invalid is the GAME's, and it is decided in\n    ///      one place: {UsingCommitReveal-_playerOf}. In the base's default,\n    ///      an address identity, it means an id that is not an account, and in\n    ///      a token game it means a token nobody has put at stake.\n    error InvalidPlayer(uint256 id);\n\n    /// @notice the player's reserve cannot cover this\n    error ReserveTooLow(uint256 current, uint256 required);\n\n    /// @notice the revealed chunk costs more than the bond still set aside\n    error BondTooLow(uint256 bond, uint256 required);\n\n    /// @notice this reveal carries more actions than one transaction may\n    /// @dev The chunk is what makes a reveal's worst case CALCULABLE, on every\n    ///      chain and whatever a game puts at stake, which is what lets a client\n    ///      pass a real gas limit instead of a guess. A final chunk allowed to\n    ///      be any length would give that back: the bound would hold for every\n    ///      reveal except the last one of every turn.\n    error TooManyActions(uint256 length, uint256 allowed);\n\n    /// @notice a reveal that promises more actions did not carry a full chunk\n    /// @dev LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN TIDY. Without it a player dribbles one\n    ///      action per transaction and spreads a turn across an unbounded number\n    ///      of reveals, which is a denial of service on the reveal phase and on\n    ///      everyone else's reads of the board. A chunk that promises a\n    ///      successor must therefore be exactly full; only the LAST one may be\n    ///      short.\n    error InvalidFurtherActions(uint256 length, uint256 required);\n\n    /// @notice a chunk size of zero, which would make every turn unrevealable\n    /// @dev Same class as a zero phase duration and refused in the same place:\n    ///      it is a deployment mistake whose cost is the first player's stake\n    ///      rather than a revert anybody sees.\n    error InvalidActionsPerReveal();\n\n    /// @notice this game's cycle is advanced by the clock and by nothing else\n    /// @dev A purely timed cycle needs no transaction at all - it simply is\n    ///      what the clock says - so there is nothing for a caller to do here\n    ///      and pretending otherwise would let one look like it had.\n    error NextPhaseNotAllowed();\n\n    /// @notice the phase durations do not describe a cycle this game can run\n    /// @dev Both phases must be non-zero on a timed policy, and both must be\n    ///      zero on a manual one. See {UsingCommitReveal} for why a zero phase\n    ///      is not a configuration but a hole: it makes a commitment either\n    ///      impossible to make or impossible to open.\n    error InvalidCycleConfiguration();\n\n    /// @notice nobody is being waited for, so unanimity has no denominator\n    /// @dev Early advance needs a closed set of members. \"Everyone has\n    ///      committed\" is not a question that can be answered under open\n    ///      entry, and answering it against an empty set would let one caller\n    ///      spin the cycle forward on their own.\n    error NoOneToWaitFor();\n\n    /// @notice this identity has not entered the game, so it cannot take a turn\n    /// @dev What entering MEANS is the game's: a funded reserve here, custody of\n    ///      a token elsewhere. What the cycle needs is only that the set of\n    ///      players who may commit is the same set unanimity is measured\n    ///      against - see {UsingCommitReveal-_makeCommitment}.\n    error NotInGame(uint256 player);\n\n    /// @notice cannot stop being a member while a turn of yours is still open\n    error CommitmentStillOpen(uint64 cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice some of the members the cycle waits for have not committed yet\n    error StillWaitingToCommit(uint64 committed, uint64 waitedFor);\n\n    /// @notice some of this cycle's commitments have not been revealed yet\n    error StillWaitingToReveal(uint64 revealed, uint64 committed);\n\n    /// @notice this game has open entry, so it has no roster to act on\n    error NoRoster();\n\n    /// @notice this game's roster was already opened\n    error RosterAlreadyOpened();\n\n    /// @notice a roster needs a creator, who is the only one who can start it\n    error InvalidCreator();\n\n    /// @notice a roster must hold at least two members\n    error InvalidSeats(uint8 seats);\n\n    /// @notice a game for a fixed set of members plays at least one cycle\n    error InvalidCycles(uint16 cycles);\n\n    /// @notice this game has played its last cycle: no commitment, advance or\n    ///         forfeit any more\n    error GameEnded(uint64 lastCycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice the game has started, so its roster is closed\n    error GameAlreadyStarted();\n\n    /// @notice every seat of this game is taken\n    error GameFull(uint8 seats);\n\n    /// @notice a game starts with at least two members seated\n    error NotEnoughMembers(uint256 seated);\n\n    /// @notice this member has acted in the current phase, so the creator\n    ///         cannot forfeit them\n    error MemberHasActed(uint256 player, uint64 cycleNumber);\n}\n","keccak256":"0x96821d387ae97a88ea2e7e6fa021d2b42e3151fa4ed2f38cd00e82f9d69928cf","license":"MIT"},"project/src/commit-reveal/interfaces/UsingCommitRevealEvents.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.21;\n\nimport {UsingCommitRevealTypes} from \"./UsingCommitRevealTypes.sol\";\n\n/// @title The events of the commit-reveal base\n/// @dev Emitted by {CommitReveal} and {UsingCommitReveal} through qualified\n///      names, and inherited by a game's own events interface so that they are\n///      in the game's ABI where a client looks for them.\n///\n///      `player` IS A `uint256` IN EVERY EVENT HERE, and it is the same\n///      `uint256` the store keys by: whatever the game means by a player\n///      (an account widened, an avatar's token id), never an address that a\n///      token game would have to truncate into.\n///\n///      NO EVENT HERE CARRIES A GAME'S ACTIONS. The base never sees them: a\n///      game emits what its actions did in events of its own, and a reader\n///      wanting whole turns stitches the chunk events below on\n///      `furtherActions`.\ninterface UsingCommitRevealEvents is UsingCommitRevealTypes {\n    /// @notice A player topped up the reserve they are willing to risk.\n    event ReserveDeposited(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        uint256 amountAdded,\n        uint256 newAmount\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A player took tokens back out of their reserve.\n    event ReserveWithdrawn(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        uint256 amountRemoved,\n        uint256 newAmount\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A player committed to a turn for this cycle.\n    event CommitmentMade(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        uint64 indexed cycleNumber,\n        bytes24 commitmentHash,\n        uint256 bond\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A player withdrew their commitment before the reveal phase.\n    event CommitmentCancelled(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        uint64 indexed cycleNumber\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A player revealed a chunk of what they had committed to.\n    /// @param commitmentHash The head this reveal opened, which for the second\n    ///        and later chunks of a turn is not the hash that was committed.\n    /// @param furtherActions The new head, or zero when this completed the turn.\n    /// @param cost What the game's resolution reported this chunk cost, taken\n    ///        from the bond and from the reserve.\n    event CommitmentRevealed(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        uint64 indexed cycleNumber,\n        bytes24 commitmentHash,\n        bytes24 furtherActions,\n        uint256 cost\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A missed reveal was settled, in whole or by one chunk.\n    /// @dev ONE EVENT FOR BOTH ROUTES, shaped like {CommitmentRevealed} because\n    ///      a settlement shown the chunks walks the chain exactly as a reveal\n    ///      does. A settlement WITHOUT them closes the commitment in one call\n    ///      and reports a zero `furtherActions`.\n    /// @param cycleNumber The cycle in progress when it was settled.\n    /// @param commitmentHash The head this settlement opened or closed.\n    /// @param furtherActions The new head, or zero when the commitment is now\n    ///        closed and any surplus of its bond is reserve again.\n    /// @param forfeited How much the game's {UsingCommitReveal-_forfeit} took,\n    ///        in the units of the bond. A game whose stake is not a bond (an\n    ///        avatar in custody) reports zero here and says what it took in an\n    ///        event of its own.\n    event CommitmentVoid(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        uint64 indexed cycleNumber,\n        bytes24 commitmentHash,\n        bytes24 furtherActions,\n        uint256 forfeited\n    );\n\n    /// @notice The cycle moved because somebody pushed it, rather than because\n    ///         the clock said so.\n    /// @dev A clock-driven turnover emits nothing, because nothing happened on\n    ///      chain: that is the difference this event exists to make visible.\n    event CycleAdvanced(\n        uint64 indexed cycleNumber,\n        bool commiting,\n        address pushedBy\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A closed roster was opened: the game now has `seats` seats, a\n    ///         creator who starts it, and plays `cycles` cycles from its start.\n    /// @param gameOptions What the game's own rules read at this table,\n    ///        opaque to the base (see {UsingCommitReveal-_gameOptions}).\n    event RosterOpened(\n        address indexed creator,\n        uint8 seats,\n        uint16 cycles,\n        bytes32 gameOptions\n    );\n\n    /// @notice A member took a seat, by funding a reserve.\n    /// @param seated How many seats are taken now.\n    event SeatTaken(uint256 indexed player, uint256 seated);\n\n    /// @notice A member left their seat: by emptying their reserve, or by\n    ///         being forfeited.\n    /// @param seated How many seats are taken now.\n    event SeatReleased(uint256 indexed player, uint256 seated);\n\n    /// @notice The creator started the game, which closes its roster.\n    /// @dev Followed by {CycleAdvanced} in the same transaction: starting\n    ///      re-anchors the clock, so the first cycle runs its full length.\n    /// @param lastCycleNumber The last cycle it plays: after it, the game has\n    ///        ended.\n    event GameStarted(\n        address indexed creator,\n        uint256 members,\n        uint64 lastCycleNumber\n    );\n\n    /// @notice The creator forfeited a member who had not acted in the\n    ///         current phase: the cycle stops waiting for them, for good.\n    event MemberForfeited(uint256 indexed player, uint64 indexed cycleNumber);\n\n    /// @notice The cycle started, or stopped, waiting for this player.\n    /// @param waitedFor Whether it now waits for them.\n    /// @param waitedForCount How many members it waits for in total, which is\n    ///        the denominator unanimity is measured against.\n    event WaitedForChanged(\n        uint256 indexed player,\n        bool waitedFor,\n        uint64 waitedForCount\n    );\n}\n","keccak256":"0x9ea182c433fe84b1f3320d9e363cab60ba8b0c746180f5780143f021aedaff30","license":"MIT"},"project/src/commit-reveal/interfaces/UsingCommitRevealTypes.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.21;\n\nimport {ITime} from \"solidity-kit/solc_0_8/debug/time/interfaces/ITime.sol\";\n\n/// @title The types of the commit-reveal base\n/// @notice Everything the mechanism means by a cycle, a commitment and a tally,\n///         and nothing a game means by an action.\n/// @dev A game's own types interface INHERITS this one, so its code and its\n///      ABI keep naming `Cycle` and `Commitment` unqualified, exactly as they\n///      did when these lived in the game. The base never sees an action type:\n///      a game's routes are typed (`reveal(player, Placement[] calldata, ...)`)\n///      and hand the base a digest and a count. See {UsingCommitReveal}.\ninterface UsingCommitRevealTypes {\n    /// @notice HOW THE CYCLE ADVANCES. One of three, chosen by the deployment.\n    /// @dev It used to be derived rather than declared: a game whose two phase\n    ///      durations were both zero was a manual game, AND was a game that\n    ///      skipped the commit phase, because one flag stood for both. Two\n    ///      independent things behind one derivation is what made this look\n    ///      like a mode instead of a policy, so the policy is now said out loud\n    ///      and the commit phase is never skipped by anybody.\n    ///\n    ///      `Timed` needs no transaction at all: the cycle simply is what the\n    ///      clock says. The other two are advanced by an `advanceCycle` route,\n    ///      which is permissionless and strictly conditional - it may only do\n    ///      what the rules already permit, so letting anyone call it grants\n    ///      nothing.\n    enum CyclePolicy {\n        /// @notice The clock decides, and nothing else can.\n        Timed,\n        /// @notice There is no clock. The cycle moves when the players have all\n        ///         acted and someone pushes it.\n        Manual,\n        /// @notice The clock decides the DEADLINE, and unanimity can bring the\n        ///         next phase forward. Never the other way round: see\n        ///         {UsingCommitReveal-_advanceCycle}.\n        TimedWithEarlyAdvance\n    }\n\n    /// @notice What the mechanism is configured with. A game's own config\n    ///         carries these plus whatever its actions need (a token, a cost).\n    struct CommitRevealConfig {\n        uint256 startTime;\n        uint256 commitPhaseDuration;\n        uint256 revealPhaseDuration;\n        ITime time;\n        /// @notice THE CHUNK: how many actions one reveal transaction may carry.\n        /// @dev A DEPLOYMENT PARAMETER AND NOT A CONSTANT, because the two things\n        ///      that decide it are both outside the framework: how expensive one\n        ///      action is to resolve (the game's) and what fits in a transaction\n        ///      (the chain's).
